refnamediv.refpurpose: NVMe over Fabrics STorage Appliance Services

refsect1.title: Introduction
refsect1.para: This page describes the services provided by the nvme-stas package.
nvme-stas is composed of two services, stafd8 and stacd8, running on a host computer (the NVMe Host).

refsect2.title: STorage Appliance Finder (stafd)
refsect2.para: The tasks performed by stafd include:

listitem.para: Register for mDNS service type _nvme-disc._tcp with Avahi, the service discovery daemon. This allows stafd to automatically locate Centralized or Direct Discovery Controllers (CDC, DDC) with zero-configuration networking (zeroconf). stafd also allows users to manually enter CDCs and DDCs as [Discovery Controller] sections of the connectivity configuration (/etc/nvme/nvme-stas.conf) when users prefer not to enable mDNS-based zeroconf.
Connect to discovered or configured CDCs or DDCs.
Retrieve the list of NVMe subsystem IO Controllers or Discovery Controller referrals from the Discovery Log Page using the NVMe command "Get Log Page".
Maintain a cache of the discovery log pages.
Provide a D-Bus API where other applications can interact with stafd. This API can be used, for example, to retrieve the list of cached discovery log pages.

refsect2.title: STorage Appliance Connector (stacd)
refsect2.para: The tasks performed by stacd include:

listitem.para: Read the list of storage subsystems (i.e., discovery log pages) from stafd over the D-Bus API.
Similar to stafd, stacd can also read a list of storage subsystems to connect to from the connectivity configuration, as [Subsystem] sections of /etc/nvme/nvme-stas.conf.
Set up the I/O controller connections to each storage subsystem.
Provide a D-Bus API where other applications can interact with stacd. For example, an application could retrieve the list of I/O controllers that stacd connected to.

refsect2.title: System configuration
refsect2.para: A host must be provided with a Host NQN and a Host ID. nvme-stas will not run without these two mandatory configuration parameters. To follow in the footsteps of nvme-cli and libnvme, nvme-stas will use the same Host NQN and ID that nvme-cli and libnvme use by default. In other words, nvme-stas will read the Host NQN and ID from these two files by default:

Using the same configuration files will ensure consistency between nvme-stas, nvme-cli, and libnvme. On the other hand, nvme-stas can operate with a different Host NQN and/or ID. In that case, one can specify them in the [Host] section of /etc/nvme/nvme-stas.conf.

A new optional configuration parameter introduced in TP8010, the Host Symbolic Name, can only be specified there: it has no system-wide file of its own. The documentation for /etc/nvme/nvme-stas.conf can be found in
nvme-stas.conf 5 .

refsect2.title: Including controllers
refsect2.para:
Both stafd and stacd can be told which controllers to connect to explicitly, instead of relying solely on mDNS discovery or Discovery Log Page Entries. A Discovery Controller for stafd is a [Discovery Controller] section, and an I/O subsystem for stacd is a [Subsystem] section, both in the connectivity configuration (/etc/nvme/nvme-stas.conf). See
nvme-stas.conf 5 .

refsect2.title: Excluding controllers
refsect2.para: Controllers that should not be connected to are excluded via libnvme's host-wide exclusion list: /etc/nvme/exclusions.conf and /etc/nvme/exclusions.conf.d/, which are managed with nvme exclusion. That list is honored by every NVMe-oF tool on the host, not just stafd and stacd, and it is read live: an entry added there takes effect on the next connection attempt, without reloading stafd or stacd.
For the design rationale behind the exclusion list, see libnvme's EXCLUSIONS.md design document.
